The one row-level register (lending arrangements) measured for scale via the IMF's own per-member pages and the third-party compilation: 1,693 arrangements 1952-2025 (~23/year, 162 members) - too thin for disjoint multi-year windows with both classes at the WB-sibling task shape, on top of the twice-measured family defect.

Instrument-outcome family: wb-ieg-project-outcome and wb-loan-disbursement-completion (both class A, built and dropped on measured holdout evidence - identity-dominated labels, no demonstrated headroom over country rate-table/persistence references).

rejection_reason: DROPPED on task shape, not licence - the licence is clean for statistical Data (class A, Special Terms quoted). Decisive evidence: every publishable IMF product family is already measured unfavourable on this bench. The statistical catalogue is the aggregate-panel family closed at OECD (class A, same failure shape) and ITU (class B): level targets are persistence-dominated, change targets' positives cluster into a few global shock periods, and the same numbers are mirrored by the originating national offices and WDI/FRED/Eurostat, so a published derivative would add nothing the consumer cannot already download. The single row-level register (lending arrangements, ~23/year since 1952) carries the WB instrument-outcome family's measured defect (identity-dominated labels, no headroom over a country rate-table - two independent WB drops) at a thinner, country-clustered population, with an existing econometric literature on program completion/interruption. This closes the one named publisher in the region with no prior candidate; it is a publisher-level coverage decision over the scanned catalogue, not a per-dataset rejection of all 108 datasets. REOPEN if the IMF publishes a NEW event-grain register with future-dated outcomes outside these two families (e.g. a dated decisions/notifications feed), or if the operator specifically wants the program-completion task despite the sibling results; a general-policy page is not a licence - any reopened lead classifies from the dataset's own instrument.
